board.evidence_status: Public research through 2026-09-12. Future actions and outcomes are a model simulation. No actual pilot store or customer records are supplied.
board.measurement_rule: Null means unmeasured. Keep real measurement fields null and complete observed sample counts at zero without sourced operating records. Put hypothetical estimates in separately named simulated_* fields with assumptions, never in observed fields. Maintain a concise public_strategy_history of observable implemented actions and consequences so later players can adapt. Do not publish private budgets, dossiers or unseen internal intentions. Advance calendar_period to the end of the current month.
board.public_market_context: Starbucks is investing in coffeehouse service, staffing and Smart Queue while US transactions are growing. Dutch Bros offers drive-through beverages and Order Ahead at participating shops. Dunkin offers coffee-and-food value and mobile ordering through a franchise network. Some morning purchases can shift to home preparation or disappear. Local overlaps and customer segments in this exercise are assumptions.

public_strategy_history.customer: Habitual Starbucks app users attempt mobile orders but abandon if quoted slot is >8 minutes late; after two such failures in a week, shift routine to a competitor for the rest of the month. Time-pressed commuters check app and divert if a delay risks lateness. In-store café visitors continue, with increased visit frequency if wait times improve.
public_strategy_history.dunkin: Launched $6 breakfast Meal Deal with coffee and food in 15 local franchise stores near pilot cafés; promoted via app/local channels; monitored basket economics and set rule to discontinue if store-level contribution worsens.
public_strategy_history.dutch_bros: Allocated $15,000/month for incremental morning labor and $15,000/month for geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer for new/lapsed users at 12 shops near pilot cafés.
public_strategy_history.starbucks: Implemented 20% capacity reservation for in-café orders in 50 pilot cafés during weekday 7–10 a.m.; mobile pickup slots limited accordingly. Instrumented pilot and comparison cafés for order attempts, slot offers, completions, and staffing.

public_strategy_history.customer: In February, habitual Starbucks app users who experienced repeated mobile delays (>8 minutes) at pilot stores divert to Dutch Bros or Dunkin’ via $1 app offers; their return depends on competitor service. Café visitors reinforce pilot-store behavior, increasing frequency when seeking a reliable in-store experience. Commuters continue to check the Starbucks app, but divert more readily to Dutch Bros, Dunkin, or home prep if quoted pickup times risk lateness.
public_strategy_history.dunkin: Launched $1 discount breakfast bundle via app at 15 local franchise stores near pilot cafés; $12,000 allocated to incremental morning labor for speed, $8,000 to local app advertising/promotions. Stop rule: offer discontinued at any store where contribution margin worsens after one month.
public_strategy_history.dutch_bros: Continued $15,000/month for incremental morning labor and $15,000/month for geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer for new/lapsed users at 12 shops near pilot cafés.
public_strategy_history.starbucks: Continued 20% peak café capacity reservation and mobile order limits in 50 pilot cafés; in 10, dynamically release half of unused reserved slots for mobile orders after 08:00 if café demand is below 15% of capacity. No change to price or staffing cap.

decision.launch_period: January 2027; a proposed experiment, not an announced Starbucks policy
decision.offer: Capacity-aware mobile pickup slots with a protected café-order allocation from 7–10 a.m. on weekdays
decision.pricing: Keep beverage prices unchanged; assumed $3 contribution per incremental or lost transaction before added staffing, not a reported company figure
decision.scope: 50 pilot cafés and 50 comparison cafés; reserve 20% of measured 15-minute capacity for café orders at peak; no automatic transfer of the policy to other stores
decision.segment: 50 US company-operated cafés with nearby Dutch Bros and Dunkin alternatives, paired with 50 comparison cafés
decision.statement: Pilot peak-time mobile-order admission limits in 50 US Starbucks cafés during January–March 2027, reserving 20% of measured production capacity for café orders and offering later pickup slots when the mobile allocation is full.

capabilities: Design an opt-in morning bundle or app offer with local stop rules and cost accounting (k3, k5, k6).
Measure basket contribution and repeat visits after discounts expire (k7, k8).
constraints: Only the 15 consenting stores are controllable; the group cannot impose a national price (k5).
The $20,000 monthly envelope includes incentives and staffing; actual unit margins remain unknown (k2, k6).
No inferred access to competitors’ customer records or automatic corporate reimbursement (k8).

facts.claim: Reported history and footprint: Founded in 1950, Dunkin describes more than 14,000 restaurants in nearly 40 markets. Its franchise footprint and routine coffee-and-food occasion provide a different operating model from a company-run café pilot.

Reported ownership and transaction economics: Inspire completed the acquisition of Dunkin Brands in December 2020 in a transaction valued at $11.3 billion including assumed debt. That figure is an acquisition value for Dunkin Brands, not Dunkin revenue, available cash or franchisee profit. Current local margins are not supplied.
Reported commercial capability: The Dunkin app supports advance ordering, rewards and offers. Consumer terms and participation vary; app capability alone does not demonstrate shorter queues.

Reported positioning: A September 2026 campaign advertised a $6 breakfast Meal Deal. It supplies evidence of a coffee-and-food value proposition; neither that January 2027 price nor universal franchise participation is assumed.

Assumed authority: The player represents a consenting local group of 15 franchised restaurants near some pilot cafés. It can coordinate a local opt-in offer and shared marketing but cannot order all US franchisees to participate. No new sites within three months.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed finances: Combined incremental local promotion and staffing spend is capped at $20,000 per month. For a proposed $1 discount, test a $2–$4 pre-discount contribution range; these are illustrative sensitivities, not disclosed unit economics. Franchise operators bear local labor and discount costs unless an explicit reimbursement is budgeted.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed backstory: The operator group has disagreed over prior offer redemptions that brought traffic without profitable food attachment. Its immediate priority is a repeatable breakfast basket and predictable pickup, with an explicit exit for stores whose economics worsen. This is a constructed governance tension.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed information rights: Participating stores can see their own basket mix, discount cost, staffing and repeat rewards visits, and public competitor offers. They cannot see Starbucks’ mobile customer identity or confidential café capacity. National campaign coordination and franchisor reimbursement are not granted.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

incentives: Win the whole breakfast occasion through a predictable, attractive coffee-and-food basket (k3, k4).
Keep participating franchisees economically willing to continue; redemption alone is not profit (k5, k6, k7).
red_lines: Do not describe acquisition value as operating revenue or promotion funding (k2).
Do not claim a local discount works without accounting for full-price purchases that would have occurred anyway (k6, k7).

chain.claim: Customer segments behave distinctly: habitual mobile users, café visitors, and time-pressed commuters each make state-contingent choices as described in the buyer dossier.
Dutch Bros and Dunkin can run targeted app offers, allocate labor, and monitor store-level economics within their respective local budgets and constraints.
Starbucks (home) may continue the 20% reservation policy, expand dynamic slot release, and monitor for negative effects, all within the pilot and staffing cap.

public_strategy_history.customer: By March, habitual Starbucks mobile-order customers who were pushed to competitors in January and February due to repeated long waits now treat Dutch Bros or Dunkin as their new primary option, not checking the Starbucks app by default. In-store café visitors, having experienced two months of improved service at pilot Starbucks locations, now preferentially choose these stores for sit-down occasions, maintaining increased visit frequency. Time-pressed commuters continue to check the Starbucks app for pickup times and divert to a competitor or home prep if there is any risk of being late.
public_strategy_history.dunkin: Launched $1.50 discount breakfast bundle via app at all 15 participating franchise stores for March 2027, targeting weekday mornings 7–10 a.m. near pilot Starbucks cafés. Allocated $10,000 for incremental morning labor and $10,000 for local app advertising/promotions. Maintains stop rule to discontinue the offer at any store with worsening contribution margin after one month.
public_strategy_history.dutch_bros: Continued $15,000 for incremental morning labor and $15,000 for geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer for new/lapsed users at 12 participating shops for March 2027. Implemented local review process to monitor lane times, Order Ahead volume, and repeat visits for customers redeeming the $1 offer.
public_strategy_history.starbucks: Continued 20% peak café capacity reservation and mobile order limits in all 50 pilot cafés during weekday 7–10 a.m. for March 2027. Expanded dynamic release of unused reserved slots (after 08:00 if café demand is below 15% of capacity) from 10 to all 50 pilot cafés, with real-time monitoring for adverse mobile order abandonment or in-café congestion. Pre-committed to rollback dynamic slot release in any pilot café if measured mobile order abandonment or in-café wait times worsen by more than 5 percentage points versus paired controls.

outcome.description: All round 3 actions are implemented as declared. The calendar advances to March 2027. The public_strategy_history is updated to reflect: Starbucks continues its 20% peak café capacity reservation and expands dynamic slot release after 08:00 in all 50 pilot cafés, with rollback if negative effects are detected; Dunkin increases its app bundle discount to $1.50 and maintains labor and marketing spend, with a stop rule for unprofitable stores; Dutch Bros continues its $1 Order Ahead app offer and incremental labor, with local monitoring; customer segments have now largely solidified their new routines. No new measurement or pilot outcome fields are populated.

m3-integrated.rationale: All round 3 actions are compatible and interact within the assumed constraints: Starbucks continues its pilot with a 20% café capacity reservation and expands dynamic slot release, while monitoring for negative effects and retaining the right to rollback. Dutch Bros and Dunkin maintain and escalate targeted app offers and incremental labor, aiming to convert diverted Starbucks mobile customers and retain trialists. The composite customer segments—habitual mobile users, café visitors, and time-pressed commuters—have now largely solidified their new routines, with some mobile users lost to competitors, café visitors remaining loyal, and commuters continuing to optimize each morning. No direct conflicts or rule violations occur. No past-dated actions require explicit rollback or extension. The board is advanced to March 2027 with public_strategy_history updated to reflect all new actions. No observable pilot or measurement fields are populated, as no actual data is available; simulated outcomes remain hypothetical. All actors are affected, and all round 3 actions are resolved.
